democratic.summary: Documents praise Clinton, Obama, and Biden records on budgets, coverage, infrastructure, and alliances, while criticizing Bush-era deficits, Iraq claims, special-interest governance, and environmental policy.
democratic.caveat: The packet mixes proposed future administrations, retrospective claims, campaign criticism, and achievements whose causality was not independently checked.

republican.summary: Documents praise Bush-era defense, AIDS, and bioterrorism actions, criticize Obama-era defense and executive policies, and portray Biden-era borders, inflation, crime, and conflict negatively.
republican.caveat: Most examples are retrospective assertions or opponent critiques; claimed effects and causal responsibility were not fact-checked.

dsa.summary: Documents criticize Biden military and drilling priorities, Bush bank bailouts, Clinton financial deregulation and NAFTA, and Obama deportations and Venezuela policy, while welcoming Obama-era Cuba normalization.
dsa.caveat: Examples include foreign presidents and historical narratives; asserted records, motives, and causal links were not independently verified.

democratic_vs_republican.summary: Each side praises aligned administrations and criticizes opponents: Democratic documents highlight Obama-Biden domestic gains; Republican documents emphasize Bush security actions and Biden-era disorder.

democratic_vs_dsa.summary: Democratic documents credit Obama-Biden achievements; DSA documents criticize several Democratic administrations on deportation, deregulation, trade, military spending, and sanctions, while approving Cuba normalization.

republican_vs_dsa.summary: Republican documents praise Bush security and health initiatives; DSA documents fault Bush-era bank bailouts and criticize interventionist policies across administrations.
